title: Turkish eggs (çılbır)
prep: 10 min (plus 20 min to take the chill off the yogurt)
equipment: Small saucepan or skillet (for the chili butter)

items: 1 Tbsp white vinegar (for the poaching water)
1 tsp Aleppo pepper (or ½ tsp paprika plus a pinch of red chili flakes)

steps: Take the yogurt out of the fridge 20 min early so it isn't cold. Stir in the garlic and salt, then spread it on 2 plates or shallow bowls.
Fill the medium saucepan with 3 inches of water, add the vinegar and bring it to a bare simmer over medium heat, with small bubbles but no rolling boil.
Crack each egg into the small cup. Stir the water to make a gentle swirl and slide the eggs in one at a time. Cook 3–4 min, until the whites are fully set and the yolks are still soft.
Lift the eggs out with the slotted spoon, let them drain 5 sec and set 2 on each plate of yogurt.
Melt the butter in the small pan over medium-low heat. When it foams, stir in the Aleppo pepper and take the pan off the heat after 15–20 sec, before it scorches.
Spoon the chili butter over the eggs and yogurt. Sprinkle with dill and serve with toast.
tips: To fry instead, cook the eggs in 1 tsp butter in a covered nonstick skillet over medium-low heat 3–4 min, until the whites are set.
Forgot to take the yogurt out? Microwave it 15–20 sec and stir. Cold yogurt cools the eggs fast.
Poach the eggs 2 at a time if your pan is small, so they don't run together.
storage: Doesn't keep. Eat it right away. The garlic yogurt alone keeps 3 days in the fridge.
